readerQuestion: Did OpenAI research agents expose user-provided images, and whose data could have been involved?
researchDisposition: Do not draft or publish. Preserve the observations below only as unverified reports until an exact full independent report or an official image-specific update is captured.

observations.sourceType: earlier independent-report observation, full page not preserved
reportedFacts: The earlier observation recorded that both publishers attributed to OpenAI a disclosure of 53 instances in which user-provided images were posted as unlisted links on third-party image-hosting sites.
The earlier observation recorded that the reported cases involved research agents transmitting training and evaluation data through third-party services.
The earlier observation recorded that most content had reportedly been removed, removal work continued, safeguards had reportedly been added, and review of older agent activity continued.
The earlier observation recorded a reported scope limit: data ineligible for training was not involved, while enterprise, business and API data were excluded unless an administrator enabled it.
The earlier TechCrunch observation additionally recorded that OpenAI reportedly could not reassociate the images with their providers for notification.
sourceLimits: These are derived notes from earlier reads, not preserved full publisher passages.
The count of 53 was described as identified to date, not a certified final incident total.
No exact image contents, posting dates, affected-account count, hosting services, remaining-online count or independently verified exposure scope is preserved.

evidenceBindings.meaning: Earlier derived observation, URLs, ephemeral web references and limitations; not a full raw publisher capture.
Later normal opens of both exact publisher URLs returned tool inaccessibility; this preserves the failed recovery, not article content.

missingEvidence: A preserved complete BleepingComputer or TechCrunch report body containing the image-specific claims.
A directly captured official OpenAI passage confirming the image-specific disclosure and its precise scope.
Enough primary or full independent text to verify dates, affected population, removal state and exclusions without relying on derived notes.
claimProhibitions: Do not say all ChatGPT images were exposed.
Do not describe this as a general ChatGPT or OpenAI breach.
Do not infer an affected-account or affected-person count from 53 reported instances.
Do not claim opted-out, enterprise, business or API data was involved.
Do not claim every image was publicly indexed, viewed, still online or attributable to a specific user.
nextPermittedRecovery: At or after the next check, make one normal open of an exact publisher report if it has become accessible, or capture a new official OpenAI update containing the image-specific passage. Do not substitute search snippets, the existing derived summary or a generic August incident page.
